title: Blue Devils all took solos, unlike other bands
summary: The Blue Devils deliberately hired soloists, while most bands, such as Twelve Clouds of Joy, had only a few.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Now, thinking about the Blue Devils... The question I'll ask you comes out of what I've been told about it, and I may be wrong -- so you correct me if I'm wrong.
Yes.
As I understand it, the Blue Devils was remarkable because it had some of the best soloists. It was a band where everybody took solos.
Yes.
Now, that's true, is it?
Yeah, that's true.
Buster Smith - 30
Now, was this because people in the band pursued that policy? That they deliberately got people in the band who could do that?
Yeah.
Or was it just a coincidence?
They wanted fellows in the band who could do that -- take solos.
There were lots of little bands like the Blue Devils, touring around, playing in dance halls and things.
Yes.
Now, in a normal band like that, how many people would normally be capable of taking solos?
Where? In the Blue Devils?
No. In the other bands?
In the other bands?
Would there only be one or two guys who could do it?
Yes, yes. Some of them had... Like, Twelve Clouds of Joy, they had three or four men in that to take solos.
Yes. But only three or four.
Yeah, yeah. Mostly it was a couple of trumpet players. I don't think they had no trombone player to take solo then. They had one then called...well, we called him Stumpy. The name is Bay.
Oh yeah, he was good.
Buster Smith - 31
Yeah, yeah. He's a New York guy. And Old Slim -- Slim Freeman. He's in Detroit, the last I heard of him.
What did he play?
He was a tenor player. He was a good tenor player.
Later on they had a guy who died, who drank a lot. A very good player. I can't remember his name. Anyway...
Oh, you're talking about Dick Wilson.
Yeah. He died of drink.
Dick Wilson, yeah.
